source: Native AWS Lambda SigV4 REST/JSON requests and AWS CLI v2 IAM/STS/CloudTrail calls

context.scope: One uniquely owned uninvoked function and two uniquely owned IAM roles; role sessions are memory-only; no versions, aliases, mappings, layers, logs, or external resource types provisioned.
context.wire_preservation: Native-signed-rest output is decoded JSON with all explicit null fields retained. Error code comes from x-amzn-ErrorType; native body capitalization and Type are retained. AWS CLI observations are separately labeled and may omit modeled null fields. HTTP 204 has an empty body represented by output {}. Signed query parameters are sorted, so repeated tagKeys wire ordering is visible separately from input.
context.redaction: Account normalized to 000000000000. Access-key identifiers, credentials, signatures and security tokens redacted. Code.Location retains HTTPS host/path and non-secret expiry/algorithm/date query parameters but all bearer-enabling values are redacted before fixture writes. Request IDs remain unchanged for audit correlation.

findings: Implemented public operation names correlate to native eventName GetFunction20150331v2, ListTags20170331, TagResource20170331v2 and UntagResource20170331v2.

Captured successful GetFunction events are readOnly true, requestParameters.functionName identifies the request, responseElements is null and resources is absent. Code.Location and returned Tags do not appear in these audit responses.

Captured successful ListTags events are readOnly true; TagResource/UntagResource are readOnly false. Their requestParameters preserve resource and tags/tagKeys. responseElements is null; successful resource projection has accountId, type function and ARN.

Direct ListTags authorization denial and successful GetFunction by the same session are independently correlated to native request IDs. Lambda-tag mutation permission errors and other recorded native failures retain errorCode/errorMessage rather than synthesized success events.

Exact function ResourceName lookups do not recover GetFunction read records, whose resource projection is absent. Exact owned-session AccessKeyId lookups recovered those records without scanning pre-existing resource identities.
cloudtrail.capture_limitations: Events are native management history available by capture_finished_at. Lookups are time-bounded to capture start/end and exact owned resource/session identities; no unobserved event or absence is inferred. Later cleanup events were not required for cleanup verification, which uses direct native GetFunction/ListTags/GetRole absence errors.

cleanup.temporary_credentials: STS sessions kept only in kernel memory; no access keys or session credentials persisted. Their issuing role and inline policy were deleted.

limitations: An initial custom-signer request for encoded ARN failed signature validation before reaching Lambda; it is excluded from service observations. Canonical URI double encoding was corrected before tag captures.

Existing explicit-allow session continued allowing direct ListTags during all 18 polling attempts after removing its role-policy ListTags Allow; do not replay those propagation observations as settled IAM semantics. Fresh-session absence and explicit-deny observations are labeled separately.

Single owned ZIP function, same account, us-east-1 only; no cross-account, Organizations/SCP/RCP, permission-boundary, function resource-policy or actual published-version/alias conclusions. Qualifiers tested without provisioning those resources.
No invocations or deployment downloads were performed in this tag capture. Code.Location only demonstrates presence and redacted structure; download behavior belongs to the separate capture.

TagsError failures could not be elicited with the tested current identity/session policies; preserve observed null and successful tag visibility rather than replacing them with documentation-derived expectations.

Role/session policies and tagged/tagless transitions are timestamped; IAM propagation attempts are retained and distinguished from settled direct-denial evidence. CloudTrail is eventually consistent and exact lookups cannot prove universal event absence.
No scratch scripts or archives were written: the Python kernel held the runner, ZIP bytes and credentials in memory. Only testdata/aws/lambda/function_tags.json was created.
findings: TagResource merges map entries, replacing exact-case keys and retaining differently cased keys; empty values are accepted. Present and absent key removals both succeed, including duplicate removal keys.

Successful real changes, identical TagResource writes and absent-only UntagResource no-ops all change public RevisionId and LastModified. Captured rejected mutations preserve tag state and both fields.

Exactly 50 tags are accepted. A merge producing 51 rejects the whole request, including an existing-key replacement in that same request. Existing-key replacement at 50 succeeds; removal then replacement addition succeeds.

Empty TagResource map is service InvalidParameterValueException with Type User. Empty UntagResource list is serialized without tagKeys and receives service ValidationException (null member). Empty key is a native ValidationException but separately a CLI ParamValidation rejection before transmission.

Only unqualified full function ARN is accepted by the three tag operations; names/partial ARNs fail ValidationException; qualified ARNs fail InvalidParameterValueException even when the qualifier is nonexistent. GetFunction accepts name/partial/full ARN and $LATEST; nonexistent version/alias returns ResourceNotFoundException.

Modeled shape validation precedes operation IAM denial; IAM denial precedes missing-resource lookup and the semantic empty-map error. For authorized caller empty TagResource map on a missing resource returns InvalidParameterValueException before ResourceNotFoundException.

Same-account native GetFunction returns Tags with TagsError null even while the identical role-session credentials are denied direct ListTags, including fresh role permission absence and explicit role/session deny. Denying GetFunction itself returns HTTP 403. This diverges from the current GetFunction documentation stating explicit lambda:ListTags allow is required; no TagsError failure was observed or fabricated.

Tagless GetFunction raw response contains Tags null and TagsError null regardless of tested ListTags allowance. AWS CLI omits these null fields. Tagless direct ListTags returns an empty map only when authorized and still returns 403 for denied credentials.

RequestTag conditions use the request, not existing matching state; TagKeys constraints are case-sensitive and mixed allowed/forbidden requests reject atomically; ResourceTag conditions use pre-mutation current state, allowing Gate=open to close/remove its own grant and denying attempts to restore it thereafter.
